title: Anaplastic_Meningioma_WGS_X10

publications.title: An integrated genomic analysis of anaplastic meningioma identifies prognostic molecular signatures

institution: Wellcome Sanger Institute / Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
needs_manual_review_reason: DEEP-AUDIT UPDATE (2026-07-14): publications[0].authors was truncated to exactly 6 names; expanded to the full 41-author list per Europe PMC authorString for PMID 30202034 (Collord G ... Santarius T, McDermott U). corresponding_author re-verified against the paper's own correspondence footnote (Europe PMC authorAffiliationDetailsList / PMC6131140 full text): the <corresp> marks two corresponding authors -- Thomas Santarius (Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, ts381@cam.ac.uk) and Ultan McDermott (Wellcome Sanger Institute, um1@sanger.ac.uk) -- confirming the existing 'Thomas Santarius / Ultan McDermott' value was already correct; no change made to that field. Full text (PMC6131140) also checked for undisclosed per-sample outcome/subtype data per this audit's brief: found a Kaplan-Meier overall-survival curve for '25 anaplastic meningioma patients in C1 and C2 subgroups', but the text explicitly ties C1/C2 to 'gene-expression defined subgroups' (RNA-seq clustering), i.e. the companion RNA-seq dataset (egas00001001873-collord-anaplastic-rnaseq), not this targeted-panel/WGS-X10 accession's own 22 patients/60 samples; also the 25-patient figure does not match this record's own 22-patient count. Left has_outcome_data and molecular_subtype_annotated unchanged for this record accordingly (the outcome/subtype evidence found belongs to a sibling EGA accession outside this audit's scope, not to EGAS00001000859 itself); flagging here only for a maintainer's awareness, not applied as a fix to this file. NEW RECORD (2026-07-11). RESOLVED MODALITY AMBIGUITY: the study title says 'WGS_X10' (suggesting whole-genome sequencing on a HiSeq X Ten instrument) but both the live EGAS00001000859 study description and its one meningioma-relevant dataset (EGAD00001001267, 'Anaplastic Meningioma WGS-X10') explicitly state 'We plan to sequence a set of 500 known cancer genes in 50 anaplastic meningioma and corresponding peripheral blood DNA samples' -- i.e. this is a targeted 500-gene cancer panel run on a HiSeq X Ten instrument, not whole-genome sequencing; 'X Ten' in the title refers to the sequencer model, not the assay. Modality is therefore set to targeted_panel_seq, not wgs, based on the live description text (dataset_types itself is null, so confidence is marked Medium rather than High). SAMPLE COUNT: live /samples endpoint for EGAD00001001267 shows num_samples=60 (38 phenotype='Brain'/tumor, 22 phenotype='Blood'/normal), mapping to 22 unique patients via the Sanger 'PD#####[a-z]' subject_id convention (root PD number = patient, suffix letter = individual sample/region), not the '50 anaplastic meningioma' originally planned per the study description (a protocol-stage estimate that appears not to match what was ultimately sequenced/deposited). MULTIPLE DATASETS UNDER ONE STUDY, TWO OF WHICH ARE OUT OF SCOPE: EGAS00001000859 actually has 3 registered datasets, confirmed live. Only EGAD00001001267 is meningioma-specific and is the basis of this record. The other two -- EGAD00001003772 and EGAD00001004203, both titled variants of 'Characterization of mutational processes/signatures in human cancer cell lines reveals episodic APOBEC mutagenesis' (163 and 192 samples respectively) -- are a pan-cancer CELL LINE mutational-signatures resource with no meningioma-specific content; they appear to share this EGAS accession as a matter of Sanger institutional/administrative grouping rather than being part of the meningioma project, and are explicitly excluded from this record (not meningioma-specific, and cell-line data would be adjacent/out-of-scope even if it were) rather than logged in related_accessions. PUBLICATION MATCH AND COHORT-SIZE DISCREPANCY: no PMID is attached in the live EGA record for any of the three anaplastic-meningioma-titled EGAS accessions in this batch (this one, EGAS00001001155, EGAS00001001873); a web search located a single integrated Wellcome Sanger Institute/Cambridge paper (PMID 30202034, Collord et al. 2018, Scientific Reports) whose PD-ID sample-naming convention, institutional authorship (Wellcome Sanger Institute, Cambridge University Hospitals), and combined WGS+targeted-panel+RNA-seq+methylation design for anaplastic meningioma appear to match all three EGAS accessions in this batch (this one, EGAS00001001155, EGAS00001001873) as sister sub-studies of the same overall project. However, the paper's own abstract/reporting describes a discovery cohort of only 18 primary tumors by WGS and a validation cohort of 31 primary tumors by a 366-gene panel, whereas the live EGA registrations in this batch show 22 patients (this dataset, 500-gene panel) + 42 patients (EGAS00001001155, 'V3' panel) + 29 patients (EGAS00001001873, RNA-seq) -- none of which numerically match the published 18/31 breakdown. This is flagged as an unresolved discrepancy between the deposited raw-sequencing patient counts (likely representing the full sequencing/recruitment funnel across panel iterations) and the smaller, QC-filtered analytic cohort actually reported in the paper's results; the publication link itself is treated as Medium confidence (found via web/citation matching rather than a direct pubmed_ids field in the EGA record) and should be independently confirmed by a maintainer. Only public EGA study/dataset-level metadata was used; the controlled-access sequencing data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md.
